lesson.text: A wave carries energy from place to place without carrying matter along: the water in a wave mostly bobs up and down.
Amplitude is how big the wave is: a bigger amplitude carries more energy (a louder sound, a brighter light). Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next.
When waves meet a material, they can be reflected (bounce off), absorbed (taken in) or transmitted (pass through).
Light is reflected by mirrors, absorbed by dark cloth and transmitted by glass. Sound reflects as an echo and is absorbed by soft curtains.

exercises.prompt: What is the amplitude of a wave?
An echo is a reflected sound.
What is the distance from one crest to the next called?
Which sound has a bigger amplitude?
exercises.explain: A shout has a bigger amplitude.

exercises.prompt: Why is a black T-shirt hotter in the sun?
exercises.explain: Dark cloth absorbs light, turning it into heat.

exercises.prompt: Why do concert halls have soft panels on the walls?
choices: to absorb sound and stop echoes

exercises.prompt: Waves carry matter all the way across the ocean.
exercises.explain: No: they carry energy; the water bobs in place.

exercises.prompt: A mirror is best at which?
Why can you hear someone around a corner but not see them?
choices: Sound spreads round corners more than light.
exercises.explain: Sound spreads round corners much more than light does.

exercises.prompt: Two waves have the same wavelength; one has twice the amplitude. Which carries more energy?
Sunglasses make things look darker. What do they do to light?
exercises.explain: They absorb part of the light.

exercises.prompt: The same material can reflect some light, absorb some and transmit some.
Order from most light transmitted to least.
